# Dr. Lyndon B. Duff

![](images/social/xv_2.jpg){fig-align="center"}

### Behavioural Ecologist Studying Social Ecology and Evolution in Carpenter Bees

I am a behavioural ecologist interested in how ecological and evolutionary processes shape social organization, cooperation, dispersal, and reproductive behaviour.

Using long-term field studies of large carpenter bees (*Xylocopa virginica*), I investigate how individual behavioural decisions scale up to population-level patterns of social structure and social evolution.

## Research Highlights

- Long-term study of facultatively social carpenter bees
- Social network analysis of bee associations
- Nest fidelity and dispersal dynamics
- Environmental drivers of reproductive behaviour
- Behavioural mechanisms underlying social evolution
